code.originalText: One-week review, seen the same day by addiction medicine: after withdrawal, a medicine for alcohol use disorder, the liver plan and recovery supports

text.paragraph: One-week review after outpatient withdrawal, seen the same day by addiction medicine. [S]

Ms. Canary returns one week after intake and is seen by Dr. Two Bulls-Harmon of addiction medicine on the same day. Her last drink was on the morning of her intake visit. The clinic nurse saw or called her every day: her CIWA-Ar was 10 on the second day with tremor, sweats and poor sleep, then fell each day to 2 today. She took the five-day gabapentin schedule as written and finished it three days ago, had the three thiamine injections, and took the potassium for five days and the magnesium as prescribed. She has had no seizures, hallucinations or confusion. Her friend stayed close during the worst days. She is eating more. The intake tests showed no HIV or hepatitis C, no hepatitis B infection or immunity, a urine test with no opioids, fentanyl or other drugs, and a negative pregnancy test. The community health worker helped her apply for Medicaid and SNAP, and she has met the peer recovery specialist once. She would like to stay off alcohol completely and wants to know about medicines that help. [S]

Follow-up: Four-week review in three weeks with blood tests, PEth, elastography and the PHQ-9. Weekly peer contact. Call the clinic, the peer specialist or 988 if needed.
